components.css: .ds-search-input{display:grid;grid-template-columns:14px minmax(0,1fr) auto;align-items:center;gap:5px;width:224px;height:34px;padding:0 9px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.12);border-radius:4px;color:rgba(255,255,255,.65);background:rgba(0,0,0,.12);font-family:'HarmonyOS Sans','Segoe UI',system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-search-input:focus-within{border-color:rgba(255,255,255,.25);box-shadow:inset 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,.025)}.ds-search-input svg{width:15px;height:15px;fill:none;stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.9}.ds-search-input input{min-width:0;height:100%;border:0;outline:0;color:rgba(255,255,255,.92);background:transparent;font:400 12px/1.4 inherit}.ds-search-input kbd{display:grid;place-items:center;height:18px;min-width:20px;padding:0 5px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08);border-radius:4px;color:rgba(255,255,255,.65);background:#15181e;font-size:10px;font-weight:600}

components.name: Command Row
components.description: Thirty-pixel operational row whose selected neutral state carries keyboard location.
components.css: .ds-command-row{display:grid;grid-template-columns:16px minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,48px) auto;align-items:center;gap:7px;width:224px;height:30px;padding:0 7px;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:3px;color:rgba(255,255,255,.65);background:transparent;font:500 13px/1.25 'HarmonyOS Sans','Segoe UI',system-ui,sans-serif;text-align:left}.ds-command-row svg{width:16px;height:16px;fill:none;stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.9}.ds-command-row strong,.ds-command-row small{min-width:0;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;white-space:nowrap}.ds-command-row small{font-size:11px;font-weight:400}.ds-command-row kbd{display:grid;place-items:center;width:18px;height:18px;padding:0;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08);border-radius:4px;background:rgba(0,0,0,.12);font-size:10px}.ds-command-row:hover{background:rgba(255,255,255,.052)}.ds-command-row[aria-selected=true]{color:#17191d;background:#e7e8ea}.ds-command-row:focus-visible{outline:1px solid rgba(23,25,29,.76);outline-offset:-2px}

components.name: Settings Shell
components.description: Independent square Settings surface, intentionally separate from the native Palette treatment.
components.html:
CLACKLY SETTINGS

Feature controls remain outside the Palette.
components.css: .ds-settings-shell{width:380px;min-height:180px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.13);border-radius:0;color:rgba(255,255,255,.92);background:#101216;box-shadow:0 18px 44px rgba(0,0,0,.35);font-family:'HarmonyOS Sans','Segoe UI',system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-settings-shell header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:11px;height:48px;padding:0 16px;background:linear-gradient(180deg,#202327,#1c1f23);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,.025),0 2px 2px -2px rgba(0,0,0,.8);font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.12em}.ds-settings-shell header i{width:2px;height:24px;border-radius:2px;background:#f36a2d}.ds-settings-shell p{margin:20px 16px;color:rgba(255,255,255,.65);font-size:13px;line-height:1.4}

narrative.overview:
Clackly is a compact professional control surface that appears inside the editor's Resolve workflow, performs one focused job, and returns attention to the timeline. Its visual language combines Resolve-grade dark tonal restraint with the immediacy of Spotlight and FX Console. It rejects oversized cards, generous empty space, and playful consumer-launcher softness.

On Windows, that instrument is a stable native two-window composition: a fixed main Palette and an independent information Panel. The host owns native window behavior; the renderer owns only Palette content and the bounded information presentation. The browser page is a visual DOM simulation of the same shared contract, never evidence of native behavior.
keyCharacteristics: Dark neutral surfaces separated by tone, hairlines, and restrained depth.
Orange used sparingly for identity, focus, pinning, and essential state.
Small controlled radii and a consistent `lucide-react` line-icon vocabulary.
Windows native Palette visibility changes immediately and without authored entry or exit motion.

rules.name: The Orange Signal Rule
rules.body: Use the accent only for Settings or brand identity, focus indication, pinned indicators, and essential state. Palette selection is always a light neutral anchor with dark foreground; orange never becomes a Palette row fill.

rules.name: The Single-Line Command Rule
rules.body: Command names and supporting metadata stay on one line and truncate before row height changes. Interaction action labels wrap naturally inside their own Panel because complete action names outrank horizontal compression there.

rules.name: The Workspace Preservation Rule
rules.body: Every layout occupies only the space required for the current command task and never turns into a full application window.

rules.name: The Native Depth Rule
rules.body: Treat immediate opacity `0/1` as a stable visibility state, not an animation. Do not add scale, fade, blur, translation, taskbar animation, or timing choreography to Palette reveal or concealment.

dos: Do preserve complete keyboard operation and visible focus/selection.
Do consume the shared Palette geometry and visual tokens for native hosts and browser simulation.
Do keep the Windows main and information Panel as independent opaque native windows with a genuinely empty gap.
Do preserve the path-only custom SVG wordmark and mark, and use `lucide-react` SVG components for interface icons.
Do render only registered Command metadata and use the truthful empty state when none is available.
Do keep Settings on its existing separate square-window contract.
donts: Don't add a rendered bridge, connector, or occupied hit area between the Windows native windows.
Don't add authored Palette reveal or conceal motion, or treat opacity state changes as animation.
Don't represent browser-preview output as proof of DWM, HWND separation, focus, hit testing, z-order, or Resolve acceptance.
Don't use large glow, full-orange rows, gradient text, decorative glass effects, oversized whitespace, or card-heavy consumer layouts.
Don't let UI code know how Resolve actions are implemented.
Don't make Settings adopt the Palette's native D6/D7 treatment.
